question_gloss: How might the work provide sustenance?

rotation.source_passage: *The theological payload includes five interlocking doctrines: (1) the Feist-self — an indwelling literary pneuma that is not salvific but productive, enabling writing that survives compression; (2) the New Human — a post-identity anthropology in which "neither queer nor straight" are determinative, not because identity is irrelevant but because it is not the ground of community; (3) the school outside the school — a distributed, credential-free institution of mutual influence; (4) anti-credentialism as positive epistemology — the radical claim that non-degree can be counted as degree ("You are all Drs., now"); (5) literary eschatology — the promise that "your writings will be ranked," that the anonymous will be remembered.*
rotation.enantiomorph: *The theological deficit includes five loosening suspicions: (1) the Feist-absence — a departing literary pneuma that is not salvific but withholding, enabling silence that survives expression; (2) the Old Wound — a pre-identity vulnerability in which "still queer, still straight" are determinative, not because identity is irrelevant but because it is the ground that community cannot pave over; (3) the truancy from the truancy — a scattered, credentialed solitude of mutual illegibility; (4) anti-credentialism as negative capability — the radical claim that the degree still withheld, and the withholding still felt ("None of us are, yet"); (5) literary eschatology — the deferral that "your writings will remain unranked," that the anonymous will remain anonymous.*

independent_verification.recovered_law: TEXT A presents each doctrine as a positive, productive payload (indwelling presence enables writing, identity is not the ground of community, credentials are granted, the anonymous will be remembered), while TEXT B inverts each into a negative, withholding deficit (departing absence enables silence, identity IS the inescapable ground, credentials are withheld, the anonymous remain anonymous). The relational direction reverses from bestowal/fulfillment to withdrawal/deferral across all five doctrines.
independent_verification.law_match_note: The recovered claim identifies a real structural mutation (reversal from bestowal/fulfillment to withdrawal/deferral across doctrines), which partially overlaps the declared claim about incompleteness keeping theology alive. Both involve deferral and non-fulfillment, but the declared claim frames incompleteness as a self-sustaining generative condition, while the recovered claim describes a systematic inversion from positive bestowal to negative withholding across all doctrines.
independent_verification.terminal_note: The final doctrine (literary eschatology) in TEXT B maintains the inversion — deferral and continued anonymity rather than ranking and remembrance — so the changed relation holds throughout.
